text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S. President Clinton invites Egyptian President Mubarak, Jordan's King Hussein, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to hold talks in Washington on the Middle East peace process. U.S. officials say the talks will deal with resuming negotiations on the Syrian-Israeli track. The White House greatly appreciates the exemplary efforts of Mubarak and Hussein.
- Syrian President Assad sends Mubarak a message on the latest developments in the peace process.

- Sudanese opposition forces take over a government garrison without bloodshed. Sudanese President Bashir says fighting is part of an Ethiopian-Eritrean-Israeli plot to enable rebel leader John Garang to take over Khartoum.
- Government and private sector to build 216,000 houses in the next financial year. The financial year begins on July 1.
- Cairo international book fair opens today.
- A pleasant suprise awaits Mubarak in the new valley.
- Mubarak holds talks with Syrian Foreign Minister Shara and Vice President Khaddam on the future of peace in the region.
- The president will today meet intellectuals and writers in the international book fair.
- Mubarak meets Khaddam and Shara and receives a message from Assad. Israeli troops withdraw from Hebron and the Palestinians rejoice in the streets.
- Sudanese opposition forces advance towards Damazine. Rebels take over three town on the White Nile and crush the government forces.
- Government considering unifying the price of cotton for local and export use to create equality between Egyptian and foreign weavers.
- Sheikh al-Azhar, head of prestigious Moslem institution, says investing money in the stock market is allowed by Islam.
- Egypt's gas reserves rise to 34 trillion cubic feet from 13 trillion in 1993.
- Court rules that sales tax should not be levied on construction companies.
